subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [Safeway Stores, Inc. v. National Union Fire Ins. Co. of Pittsburgh, Penn., supra, 64 F3d at 1289 (applying Calif. law)—defense costs “reasonably related” to defense of insured directors and officers must be paid by D&O insurer even if payment benefits uninsured party (the corporation)] (2) [3:710] Allocation of settlement costs: When a settlement resolves both covered and noncovered claims, the insurer may attempt to allocate the settlement amounts. (a) [3:711] Allocation denied unless “larger settlement” due to uninsured claim: Several courts have allowed a corporation to obtain reimbursement of all settlement costs where its liability is purely derivative of the liability of its insured directors and officers. Allocation is appropriate only to the extent settlement and defense costs were increased due to corporate liability that is not “concurrent” with the liability of its directors and officers.
